brief: Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities escalated Middle East tensions and pushed Brent to cycle highs near $100, with WTI spiking toward $94 after reports the US hit Iranian targets near Kharg Island. Capital Economics and Goldman Sachs raised oil estimates on expectations of prolonged shipping disruption through Hormuz and the Red Sea. Unlike prior episodes, no reflexive diplomatic dip followed; Rystad said markets overstated how much midterm politics would push Trump toward a deal. Gasoline and diesel hit record highs for Labor Day. The late crude spike snapped Treasury yields higher (2-3bps vs Friday) and pushed the S&P and Dow toward session lows, Dow dragged by Amgen. Nasdaq still outperformed, buoyed by a massive short squeeze and a second straight day of momentum reversal (Goldman's basket +15% from Thursday's lows) plus OpenAI's Astra launch lifting the Broad AI basket over the S&P ex-AI. Elsewhere: Waller's disinflation comments raise the stakes for Friday's CPI ahead of next week's FOMC; the yen strengthened on Japanese wage data, reinforcing BOJ tightening bets; Brazilian markets rallied on EWZ call demand tied to Lula's election odds; gold and bitcoin both fell. Goldman data shows AI adoption rising only linearly, undercutting a "rapid adoption" narrative.
